body:
> Replaces #397
> 
> 6 of 6.
> 
> ### Prerequisites, as the first three commits
> - Duplicate and paste rewrite ids only, not every UUID-shaped string.
> - A note keeps its id across a save.
> - SuperShape's N31 keeps its negative default across a save.
> 
> ### Clone sets
> - A set holds one stored graph, and its members are instances of it.
> - When an edit's undo group closes, the edited member becomes the stored graph and each sibling is patched to it, inside the same group. Undo and redo put siblings back with the edit.
> - A changed node takes the stored settings through `Graph.setSettings`, in place. Nodes are never remade, so untouched nodes keep their objects and runtime state.
> - Published inlet values stay each member's own.
> - Node menu: Duplicate as Clone, Rename Clone Set, Select Sibling Clones, Unlink from Clones. The breadcrumb shows a linked glyph.
> 
> ### Tests
> `CloneSetContractTests` and `CloneSetTests`, 120 tests, with no known issues.
title: Clone Sets – Sub graphs can be cloned within a document

body:
Genie –

> Closes #399 · Implements #328 step 7
> 
> 5 of 6.
> 
> ### What it establishes
> - **The node declares.** `declaredPorts()` returns the node's whole interface as an ordered list, computed from its settings, with no side effects.
> - **The registry reconciles.** `PortRegistry.reconcile` keeps matching ports, replaces retyped ones in place under the same id and position, adds missing ones and removes the rest. It returns a diff, and no longer touches the graph.
> - **The node applies the diff.** `reconcilePorts()` passes it to the graph: wires, publishing events, and the parameter group rebuilt in port order.
> 
> Equal settings give equal ports, in equal order, under equal ids for surviving keys, however the node got there.
> 
> Every node is migrated. Removed: `removePort`, `replacePort`, `reorderPorts`, the base-class port helpers, 26 static name sets and about 35 hand-kept order lists. `addDynamicPort` is deprecated.
> 
> The only exception: Math Expression, JavaScript and Live Image keep the interface of the last source that compiled, so a half-typed edit keeps its wires.
> 
> ### Tests
> - `DeclaredPortsInvariantTests` runs over 50 node types through seeded sequences of settings changes, undos and redos. After each step it compares ports with a node opened from the current settings.
> - A test opens a document saved with drifted port order, and checks it reads in declared order with every wire kept.
> 
> ### Not in this PR
> - Clone sets (#6).
title: Ports – A node's ports are reconciled to the interface it declares

body:
> 4 of 6.
> 
> Create Subgraph becomes one `performEdit` group of public API calls: unpublish moved ports, delete, add the subgraph node, add the moved nodes inside it, connect, publish the boundary ports and connect onto their proxies. Undo and redo are the group's own steps.
> 
> `SubgraphEmbedding`, its bespoke undo pair and the topology batching go, along with the `disconnect` flag on `delete(node:)`. That is −218 lines in `Graph.swift`.
> 
> A boundary port no proxy can stand for is refused up front, with nothing changed. Published names carry over, and a started node stays started.
> 
> AGENTS.md: every edit registers, and nothing inside a compound edit suspends registration.
> 
> ### Not in this PR
> - Declared ports (#5).
> - Clone sets (#6).
title: Graph – Create Subgraph is one undo group of ordinary edits

body:
Genie –

> Closes #401 · Supersedes `NodeSettingsSession` from #396
> 
> 3 of 6.
> 
> ### What it establishes
> - A node with settings exposes them as one `NodeSettings` value, through `settings` and `apply(_:)`, and offers `init(context:settings:)`. The value is saved flattened under the node's existing keys, so documents are unchanged.
> - `Graph.setSettings` records one step: the settings either side, and the states of the ports the change touched. Wires and proxies register their own steps in the same group.
> - Settings views hold a draft and commit it. Pickers and steppers commit on each change; text and code commit after a pause and when editing ends. Code editors record no typing undo of their own, so the draft is the only record.
> - Every node with settings is migrated: Strategy, Routing, Format String, Math Expression, Parametric Geometry, JavaScript, Live Image, Timeline, the device nodes, the local model nodes and Deferred Render.
> - The Fabric Editor's Undo and Redo go through the root graph, with their menu state cached from notifications.
> 
> ### Not in this PR
> - Create Subgraph through the public API, and the "every edit registers" rules in AGENTS.md (#4).
> - Port order as a function of settings (#5).
> 
> ### Temporary lines
> - `apply(_:)` still rebuilds a node's ports, and `PortRegistry.register` and `remove` carry restore states. Both are replaced in #5.
> 
> ### Note for merging
> If `fix/string-split-separator` lands first, change its test's two `node.strategy = …` lines to `node.setStrategy(…)`.
title: Settings – A node's settings are one value it gives and applies

body:
Genie –

> Closes #400 · Supersedes the proxy fixes in #395 and #396
> 
> 2 of 6.
> 
> ### What it establishes
> - The inner graph tells its `SubgraphNode` of each change through four events: `portDidPublish`, `portWillUnpublish`, `port(_:wasReplacedBy:)` and `portDidRename`. `onPublishedPortsChanged` and the after-the-fact proxy diff go.
> - Several levels of publishing are handled by recursion through the public API. Proxy-chain state and `reattachConnections` are gone.
> - `rebindWires(from:to:)` keeps each wire that `canConnect` allows and disconnects the rest, as undoable steps. Same-type replacements retarget the proxy in place.
> - `Port.published` and `publishedName` are read-only outside Fabric. Changes go through `Graph.setPublished` and `setPublishedName`.
> - Insert Parameter Node moves out of auto layout into a file of its own, and its publish transfer becomes undoable.
> 
> ### Not in this PR
> - Settings values, and the replaced-port tests that change a strategy (#3).
> - Create Subgraph through the public API (#4).
> - Clone members' own proxy ids (#6).
> 
> ### Temporary lines
> - `addDynamicPort`, `removePort` and `replacePort` raise the events. Declared ports replace them in #5.
> - BaseImageNode's legacy port merge, which goes in #5.
> - Two embedding lines, which go in #4.
> - `proxyID(for:)` returns the inner port's id. It changes in #6.
title: Publishing – A subgraph node owns its proxies, and is told each change as the change it is

body:
Genie –

> Supersedes the undo half of #396 · Design reference: [PUBLISHING_AND_SETTINGS.md](link)
> 
> 1 of 6. Each layer is final-state code: nothing here is removed by a later PR, except the temporary lines listed below.
> 
> ### What it establishes
> - Undo steps register through `Graph.registerUndo` on the graph the edit was made in, and resolve the root's undo manager when a sub graph has none of its own. `UndoRegistrationTests` fails any core code that registers on the undo manager directly.
> - A step holds ids and values, and finds what it acts on by id when it runs.
> - Compound edits run through `performEdit(named:)`, which keeps the edit's name through undo and redo. Single steps name their inverse pair with `nameEdit`.
> - Publishing, renaming a published port, notes and parameter values set through controls are undo steps.
> - `Graph.undo()` and `redo()` commit a control's change held for a pause first, so an undo never passes over it.
> 
> ### Not in this PR
> - Proxy handling and the closed `published` setter (#2).
> - Settings as values and the Fabric Editor's Undo and Redo commands (#3).
> - Create Subgraph keeps its embedding with suspended registration until #4, so "nothing inside a compound edit is suppressed" is added to AGENTS.md there.
> 
> ### Temporary lines
> - Two `registerUndo` calls in the old Create Subgraph embedding, and the `disconnect` flag on `delete(node:)`. Both go in #4.
> - `registerUndo(on:)` in StrategyNode's `strategy` didSet. It goes in #3.
> - One `ParameterGroupView` line. It changes in #6.
title: Undo – Every edit registers through the graph that made it
